name: What foundation is best for a family-room addition?

mainEntity.name: Should a family-room addition use a slab, crawlspace, or raised foundation in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Should a family-room addition use a slab, crawlspace, or raised foundation in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Foundation choice is a major design and cost decision for a family-room addition. A slab foundation can be efficient and cost-effective when the site is relatively level and the house design allows it. A raised foundation may be better when the existing home sits above grade, when plumbing or access needs matter, or when the lot has slope or drainage challenges. In many Los Angeles neighborhoods, matching the existing house elevation is important so the new room does not feel like an afterthought. Soil conditions, seismic considerations, and grading can also affect the decision. The best foundation is the one that supports the addition structurally while minimizing future movement, moisture issues, and awkward floor transitions.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best foundation depends on soil conditions, grading, existing house elevation, and drainage. A slab is often simpler and cheaper, while a raised foundation can help match an older home or manage site slope and access issues.
